cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Take my good teacup. It'll remind you of our afternoons wherever you end up. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I end up elsewhere?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Someone as capable as you must have wonderful doors waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you asking me to leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm making sure you won't mistake this doorway for your last opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my good teacup. It'll remind you of our afternoons wherever you end up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I end up elsewhere?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone as capable as you must have wonderful doors waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you asking me to leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm making sure you won't mistake this doorway for your last opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed extra sandwiches for your journey. You always forget to eat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only visiting the next town.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they'll keep you well as long as you choose to stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That sounds very final.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only because I want the last thing you hear here to be kindness.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The lift costs petrol and a proper conversation about why you stopped calling. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for petrol.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Good. That gets the car moving, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss it another day?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today costs petrol and another postponed conversation. The second price is rising.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift costs petrol and a proper conversation about why you stopped calling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for petrol.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. That gets the car moving, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss it another day?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today costs petrol and another postponed conversation. The second price is rising.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow the dress for ten pounds and an acknowledgment that you mocked it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Money covers fabric. It doesn't cover wearing my bad taste proudly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. It's beautiful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now say which part of my judgement improved since yesterday.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I said I'd carry one box. That warehouse isn't the box. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to help me move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. With one box. We admired how manageable the sentence was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it the biggest one, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. The word 'one' has retained its dignity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I said I'd carry one box. That warehouse isn't the box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to help me move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With one box. We admired how manageable the sentence was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it the biggest one, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. The word 'one' has retained its dignity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I agreed to watch your dog today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow's only a few hours away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A separate word with no place in our agreement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you loved dogs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An enduring feeling, not a calendar extension.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You said 'nothing can go wrong' before balancing the key on the teacup. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fell into the cup. I dried it with the invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. And now the invitation has dissolved around the key to the wedding hall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can still prise it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Your 'nothing' has become both the lock and the address we can't read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said 'nothing can go wrong' before balancing the key on the teacup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fell into the cup. I dried it with the invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now the invitation has dissolved around the key to the wedding hall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can still prise it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Your 'nothing' has become both the lock and the address we can't read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember calling the spare chair unnecessary before giving its place to the cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake needed somewhere flat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the guest sat on the piano stool, and you moved the pianist to the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's managed perfectly well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until we open that window to cool the cake. Every sensible decision is now sitting on the next one.
